claims.claim: Formulas: HPR = (P1 − P0 + D)/P0; cumulative = product of (1 + r) over k periods − 1; annualized = (1 + cumulative)^(1/t) − 1 with t = years = k ÷ periods per year; sample standard deviation (n−1, n = observations); Sharpe = (Rp−Rf)/σp; Treynor = (Rp−Rf)/βp; Jensen alpha = Rp − [Rf + βp(Rm−Rf)]; active (relative) return = Rp − R_benchmark
claims.basis: standard textbook formulas; σ convention stated as sample (n−1), population form (÷ n) noted as used in E6; annualization applied only when t > 1 (GIPS: returns for periods under one year must not be annualized); 'excess return' usually means Rp − Rf (consistent with E4), some texts use Rp − R_benchmark

claims.claim: Worked example (Ambrose Pemberton-Hale; renamed from Leo in v1.1 for name uniqueness): buy $40, $1 dividend, end $43 → HPR 10% [fix round 1: example moved under '### Rate of return' together with the linking/annualizing example]
Worked example: returns 6, 10, 14 → mean 10, σ 4% (sample); population convention gives 3.27%
Worked example: two annual returns +20% then −10% → 8% cumulative, t = 2 years, 3.92% annualized, vs 5% arithmetic mean

Worked example: Rf 3, Rm 8, market σ 12. Fund A 10%, σ15, β1.2 → Sharpe 0.47, Treynor 5.83, alpha +1.0. Fund B 9%, σ20, β0.8 → Sharpe 0.30, Treynor 7.50, alpha +2.0. Market Sharpe 0.42, Treynor 5.0; Treynor units = percentage points of excess return per unit of beta; market beta = 1 by definition
Interpretation: B high σ relative to β signals unsystematic risk; Sharpe for a sole/whole portfolio, Treynor/Jensen for a component of a diversified portfolio
claims.basis: standard interpretation of Sharpe vs Treynor/Jensen

claims.claim: Benchmark example: 60/40 blend of 8% and 3% = 6%; fund 7% → +1% active (relative) return

Multi-factor regression (Fama–French three-factor form): Rp − Rf = α + β1(Rm − Rf) + β2·SMB + β3·HML + ε; α = return not explained by the factors, an estimate of skill subject to luck and model choice; loadings = style
claims.basis: Fama–French three-factor model (1993); alpha is a regression estimate (noise, omitted factors); conceptual only

claims.claim: Higher Sharpe/Treynor/alpha is better only when compared over the same period and Rf; negative Sharpe means return below risk-free
claims.basis: standard interpretation; Rp < Rf ⇒ numerator negative

claims.quote: Any written or electronic communication for client use which contains a recommendation relating to a security or derivative, or trading strategy

claims.claim: Definition: correspondence
claims.quote: Any advertisement or business related communication, including any written or electronic communication, prepared for distribution to a single current or prospective client

claims.claim: Content and purpose, not distribution method, decide the category
claims.quote: Whether materials are considered correspondence, advertising or sales literature is determined by their content and purpose rather than how they are distributed.

claims.claim: First use of a template advertisement needs pre-approval
claims.quote: The first use of a template advertisement requires pre-approval.

claims.claim: Minor template changes (e.g. RR name, branch location) need no approval
claims.quote: minor changes to the template such as the name of the Registered Representative or location of the branch do not require approval

claims.claim: Cross-supervision: no one approves or supervises their own materials
claims.quote: An individual should not be responsible for approval or supervision of their own materials.

claims.claim: 3602(1) lead-in: must not issue, participate in or knowingly allow use of its name
claims.quote: A Dealer Member must not issue, participate in or knowingly allow the use of its name in any advertisement, sales literature or correspondence that:

claims.claim: Unrepresentative statistics, including failure to identify material assumptions
claims.quote: uses unrepresentative statistics to suggest unwarranted or exaggerated conclusions, or fails to identify the material assumptions made in arriving at these conclusions

claims.claim: Detrimental to the interests of the public, CIRO or its Dealer Members
claims.quote: is detrimental to the interests of the public, the Corporation or its Dealer Members

claims.claim: Fails to comply with CIRO requirements or applicable laws
claims.quote: fails to comply with Corporation requirements or any applicable laws

claims.claim: Records must demonstrate compliance with misleading communications requirements; prose links this to IDPC 3640 (Part C 'Misleading communications') as well as 3602(1)
claims.quote: demonstrate compliance with misleading communications requirements

claims.claim: Explanation (not a stated rule purpose): communications shape what clients believe, which is one reason the dealer must supervise them; clients use titles to judge expertise; harm of a misleading message comes before any trade
claims.basis: purpose statements; consistent with Notice 14-0073 (vulnerable/less sophisticated investors) and IDPC 3640(1)

claims.claim: Off-channel consequence: an uncaptured chat about a client's account is a retention and supervision risk; the dealer cannot use it to show compliance
claims.basis: inference from GN-3600-21-002 retention/retrieval passages (L277-279), IDPC 3804(2)(xiii)-(xiv) record duties and Compliance Report 2026 s.3.5 (all quoted)

claims.claim: Scenario (Seraphine Taillefer, 'President's Circle Advisor' on LinkedIn; award given to top revenue producers): barred by 3640(2)(i); profile is static content needing pre-approval
claims.basis: application of quoted IDPC 3640(2)(i) and GN-3600-21-002 static-content passage (L232)

claims.claim: Scenario (Radomir Volkov texts sell instruction to RR's personal messaging app, unapproved): business record on any device; she must preserve it in the dealer's records as firm policy directs; she should confirm the instruction through an approved channel before acting; tell client to use approved channels (guidance: discourage e-mail orders)
claims.basis: application of quoted GN-3600-21-002 L277 (content decides; device irrelevant; 'captured by this requirement'), GN-3600-21-002 'Client Orders' L203 and Compliance Report 2026 s.3.5; 'confirm before acting' is presented as the prudent step (should), not as a quoted rule

claims.claim: Records must properly record business activities, financial position, operating results and client transactions
claims.quote: properly record its business activities, financial position, financial operating results and client transactions

claims.claim: Records must demonstrate compliance with securities laws and CIRO requirements
claims.quote: demonstrate the Dealer Member’s compliance with securities laws and Corporation requirements

claims.claim: Internal controls: records correct, clear and accurate, current
claims.quote: A Dealer Member must maintain appropriate internal controls to provide reasonable assurance that its records: (i) are correct, (ii) provide clear and accurate information, and (iii) remain current.

claims.claim: Account appropriateness determination before opening an account, on a reasonable basis, client interest first
claims.quote: Before a Dealer Member opens an account for a person , the Dealer Member must determine, on a reasonable basis and putting the person’ s interest first, that:

claims.claim: Appropriateness covers the account itself
claims.quote: this action is appropriate for the person

claims.claim: Appropriateness covers scope of products, services and account relationships
claims.quote: the scope of products, services and account relationships which the person would have access to within the account are appropriate for the person

claims.claim: OEO and DEA accounts exempt from the scope test
claims.quote: Clause 3211(1)(ii) does not apply in respect to: (i) an order execution only account, or (ii) a direct electronic access account.

claims.claim: Dealers must explain account types' features and costs (fee-based vs commission-based) and recommend the type that puts client interest first
claims.quote: also explain the features and associated costs of the different types of accounts that are available to the client at the Dealer, such as, for example, fee-based and commission-based accounts, as applicable, and recommend the type of account that puts the client’s interest first.

claims.claim: Records must demonstrate KYC (and KYP/PDD) compliance, so KYC updates, periodic reviews and the client's confirmation belong on file; KYP and PDD both named in 3804(2)(xii)
claims.quote: demonstrate compliance with know-your -client, account appropriateness, product due diligence, know-your-product and suitability determination requirements

claims.claim: Disclosure alone never satisfies the conflicts rule (3111(1)/3112(1)); cross-element consistency X03 with E1 1.23
claims.quote: A Dealer Member and an Approved Person do not satisfy subsections 3111(1) or 3112(1) solely by providing disclosure to the client.

claims.claim: Supporting history (pre-dates IDPC 3113(3)): specific measures such as firm-wide controls and documented best-interest assessments
claims.quote: In most cases, conflicts cannot be addressed through disclosure alone; Dealers should take specific measures such as firm-wide controls and/or documenting best-interest assessments made by the Dealer’s representatives.

claims.claim: The notice generally considers a product-neutral grid a best practice
claims.locator: IIROC Notice 17-0093 'Compensation bias in favour of fee-based accounts', ~L285
claims.quote: Most Dealers stated that their compensation grid is product-neutral, which we generally consider to be a best practice.

claims.claim: Scenario (client inherited shares and transferred them into her account; supervisor queries the concentration; RR answers by phone; nothing written): review not complete — the transfer-in was a 3402(2)(i) trigger, so a suitability review must cover the concentration (3402(1)(i)(c)) and the sale plan; the dealer must record and keep evidence of the inquiry and its resolution (3927(2))
claims.basis: application of quoted IDPC 3402(2)(i) (claim 114), 3402(1)(i)(c) (claim 119) and 3927(2) (claim 96)

claims.claim: Annualize only a period longer than one year; for a shorter period report the cumulative (not annualized) return
claims.basis: GIPS convention (returns for periods of less than one year must not be annualized); annualizing a 5% quarter as (1.05)^4 − 1 = 21.6% would overstate performance

claims.claim: Product due diligence includes monitoring approved securities for significant changes (context for the GN-3300-21-001 passage)
claims.quote: monitor the securities or derivatives for significant changes

claims.claim: 3402 (incl. the 3402(2) trigger-event review) does not apply to order execution only or direct electronic access accounts, other than 3402(3)(i)
claims.quote: Other than clauses 3402(3)(i) and 3403(4)(i), sections 3402 or 3403 do not apply in respect to: (i) an order execution only account, or (ii) a direct electronic access account.

claims.claim: The 3402(1) test includes that the action puts the retail client's interest first
claims.quote: the action puts the retail client’s interest first

claims.claim: Performance report condition: account with a debit or credit balance or positions, or reportable outside holdings
claims.quote: holds one or more outside holdings for which quarterly reporting pursuant to section 3809 is required

claims.claim: Performance report condition: account with a debit or credit balance
claims.quote: a debit or credit balance, or

claims.claim: Performance report condition: at least one position or outside holding with a determinable market value
claims.quote: there is at least one position in the account or at least one outside holding for which quarterly reporting pursuant to section 3809 is required, for which a market value can be determined

claims.claim: The performance report gives combined information about the client's account and outside holdings (account-level, not per fund)
claims.quote: The annual performance report must include all of the following combined information about the client’s account and outside holdings

claims.claim: The trailing commission notice is required only if the dealer received trailing commissions on the client's securities
claims.quote: if the Dealer Member received trailing commissions related to securities owned by the client during the period covered by the report

claims.claim: Who 3640(1) binds: the Approved Person, and the dealer (itself or its Approved Persons), including through a trade name
claims.quote: An Approved Person must not hold themselves out, and a Dealer Member must not hold itself or its Approved Persons out, including through the use of a trade name

claims.claim: IDPC 3640 is the IDPC section titled 'Misleading communications' (Part C)
claims.quote: 3640. Misleading communications

claims.claim: Dealers should at least monitor or prohibit electronic communications that are recommendations
claims.quote: At the very least Dealers should implement measures to monitor and/or prohibit electronic communications that constitute a recommendation

claims.claim: Performance material should be reviewed for compliance with NI 81-102 (replaces unsupported 'fund sales communications have their own rules')
claims.quote: These materials should be reviewed for compliance with section 3603 and NI 81-102.

claims.claim: A business-related communication is captured by the retention requirement whatever the device
claims.quote: and therefore captured by this requirement, depends on the content of the communication

claims.claim: Dealers should discourage clients and RRs from sending orders by e-mail
claims.quote: Dealers should discourage clients and Registered Representatives from using e-mails to communicate orders.

claims.claim: Account appropriateness: some accounts are fully exempt from 3211(1), e.g. accounts held by a bank
claims.quote: an account held by a Dealer Member , regulated entity, exempt market dealer, portfolio manager, bank, trust company or insurance company

claims.claim: Client must be asked to confirm the accuracy of KYC information within a reasonable time
claims.quote: Within a reasonable time after receiving the information collected under subsection 3202(1), a Dealer Member must take reasonable steps to have a client confirm the accuracy of such information.

claims.claim: Unsuitable client instruction: the dealer may carry it out only after the 3402(5) steps
claims.quote: if a Dealer Member receives an instruction from a retail client to take an action that, if taken, does not satisfy subsections 3402(1), the Dealer Member may carry out the retail client’s instruction if the Dealer Member has

claims.claim: Step 1: inform the client of the basis for the determination and advise against proceeding
claims.quote: informed the retail client of the basis for the determination that the action will not satisfy subsection 3402(1) and advised the client against proceeding with the order

claims.claim: Step 2: recommend an alternative action that satisfies 3402(1)
claims.quote: recommended to the retail client an alternative action that satisfies subsection 3402(1)

claims.claim: Step 3: recorded confirmation of the client's instruction to proceed
claims.quote: received recorded confirmation of the retail client’s instruction to proceed with the action

claims.claim: Definition: Registered Individuals = Registered Representatives, Portfolio Managers and Associate Portfolio Managers
claims.quote: the term “Registered Individual” refers collectively to individuals approved by IIROC as Registered Representatives, Portfolio Managers or Associate Portfolio Managers

claims.claim: Product due diligence is the dealer's duty
claims.quote: A Dealer Member must not make securities or derivatives available to clients unless the Dealer Member has taken reasonable steps to

claims.claim: KYP is the Approved Person's own duty: take steps to understand the security before buying, selling or recommending
claims.quote: An Approved Person of a Dealer Member must not purchase or sell securities or transact in derivatives for, or recommend securities or derivatives to, a client unless the Approved Person takes steps to understand the securities

claims.claim: Ongoing suitability of the scope of account relationships (account type), on a reasonable basis and client interest first
claims.quote: the scope of products, services and account relationships which the retail client has access to within the account are suitable for the retail client

claims.claim: Buy-and-hold clients in fee-based accounts can pay ongoing fees without commensurate service
claims.locator: IIROC Notice 17-0093 'Compensation bias in favour of fee-based accounts', ~L277
claims.quote: there are other cases such as “buy and hold” where the client will be paying ongoing fees without receiving a commensurate level of ongoing service

claims.claim: Sales practices: overly aggressive sales targets can lead to inappropriate sales activity
claims.quote: It is also possible that inappropriate sales activity will result from a Dealer setting overly aggressive sales targets that representatives must meet.

claims.claim: Sales practices: examiners will ask for the rationale behind sales targets and the controls on them
claims.quote: BCC will ask Dealers to explain the rationale behind sales targets and controls they have implemented to guard against inappropriate sales activity.

claims.claim: A neutral grid gives no financial motive to favour a product or account type
claims.quote: Compensation programs should be designed in such a way that there is no financial motivation to bias a representative towards either specific products or specific account types.

claims.claim: Many dealers paid performance bonuses linked to fee-based assets
claims.quote: a significant number of Dealers provide additional incentives to representatives in the form of performance bonuses linked to fee-based assets

claims.claim: A biased incentive favouring related-party products magnifies a conflict rather than addressing it
claims.quote: by providing a biased financial incentive to favour related-party products over comparable third-party products, the Dealer is magnifying, rather than addressing, a conflict of interest

claims.claim: Why sales/compensation/incentive records matter: pay can bias advice, so a biased incentive creates a conflict (explanation, not rule text); separately, records must demonstrate compliance with conflicts requirements (3804(2)(xvi), see R claim)
claims.basis: explanation linking quoted IDPC 3804(2)(xvi)-(xvii) and Notice 17-0093 findings
